what: Performance budgets. Exceeding one fails `npm run perf`, and so the Performance CI job.
measuredOn: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest, the Performance job, Chromium headless, OCR served from the pinned cache
basis: fb8238e — Performance job, read from its CI log on 2026-10-03
rule: budget = max(2 × worst observed p95, worst observed p95 + 15 ms), rounded up to the next 5 ms
why: p95 over 20 samples (two passes in opposite order) tolerates one slow sample and not two; a single max would gate on one GC pause.

Across the three CI runs the worst p95 moved by up to 23% (floor: 178.9 → 220.5 ms). Twice the WORST run leaves room for that runner noise and still fails on a doubling — the size of regression an O(n) step becoming O(n²), or a render doing its work twice, produces.
Below ~15 ms the runner's own jitter (timer, GC) is a large fraction of the number, so a small operation gets an absolute 15 ms floor rather than a ratio no one could hold.
These are regression budgets on a 3,000-guest / 400-table / 4,000-chair stress event (§26's minimum), not promises about a typical event, which is several times smaller.
Re-deriving a budget is a deliberate, explained edit to this file — never a change made to turn a red run green.

analysis.what: Assisted Detection with OCR on the real venue plan, median of 3 runs, wall clock from the click

seatingSeries.what: 300 renders of the busiest screen: median of the last three blocks of 25 over the median of the first three
seatingSeries.why: A leak climbs; noise does not trend. Single blocks have doubled and recovered (§26), so a ratio of three-block medians, not one block.

domGrowth.what: DOM nodes after three laps of every screen minus after one lap
domGrowth.why: The count is deterministic; any growth is nodes left behind.

saveDrain.what: 40 back-to-back saves of the 4,000-seat event through the queue, until the last value is the record on disk (read back included)
